criteria.text: Adult and pediatric patients with β-thalassemia who require regular red blood cell (RBC) transfusions (FDA indication; approval criterion 3).
Patient is 4 years of age or older (approval criterion 1).
Prescribed by or in consultation with a hematologist (approval criterion 2).
Diagnosis of β-thalassemia confirmed by genetic testing (approval criterion 3).
Patient weighs a minimum of 6 kg (approval criterion 4).
Able to provide adequate cells to meet the minimum recommended dose of 5.0×10^6 CD34+ cells/kg (approval criterion 5).
Negative tests for HBV, HCV, HIV, and HTLV-1&2 prior to collection of cells (approval criterion 6).
Documented history of ≥100 mL/kg/year of pRBCs in the immediately preceding two years OR ≥8 transfusions of pRBCs in the immediately preceding two years (approval criterion 7).
No previous gene therapy for transfusion-dependent thalassemia (TDT) (denial criterion 2).
No previous allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplant (HSCT) for TDT (denial criterion 3).

notes: Partial encoding of Alaska Medicaid Zynteglo (betibeglogene autotemcel), autologous hematopoietic stem cell-based gene therapy for transfusion-dependent β-thalassemia. Version: 1; Original: 10/9/2024; Accepted: 11/15/2024; Effective: 01/01/2025. The PDF heading spells the generic betibeglogene-autoemcel.
Encoded: FDA indication, approval criteria 1-7 and denial exclusions 2-3. Denial criterion 1 (failure to meet approval criteria) is covered by the approval clauses.
Duration (notes only): initial approval up to 6 months; no reauthorization will be approved.
Quantity (notes only): one infusion per lifetime; HCPCS J3393. No numeric quantity enforcement; max_units is null.

Cautions (notes only): monitor platelet and neutrophil counts following infusion due to delayed or failed engraftment risk. Monitor for hematologic malignancy at least annually for a minimum of 15 years following infusion.

Cautions (notes only): avoid antiretroviral medications or hydroxyurea beginning a minimum of one month, or for the expected duration of elimination of all such medications, prior to mobilization until all cycles of apheresis are completed.

Cautions (notes only): discontinue iron chelators seven days before myeloablative conditioning and avoid until six months after Zynteglo infusion. Dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) may cause hypersensitivity reactions, including anaphylaxis.

Remaining gaps: documentation verification, duration, no reauthorization, lifetime quantity enforcement and monitoring require manual review. Genetic confirmation, adequate CD34+ cell dose, infectious testing and transfusion history are attestations.
PDL status unknown. No evaluate-linked alternatives.
